bangla_explanation: ভালো facilitator নিজে প্রশ্ন করে, learners-দেরও প্রশ্ন করতে উৎসাহ দেয়।
সাত ধরনের প্রশ্ন: open, closed, direct, indirect, leading, factual, probing।
Open question আলোচনা বাড়ায়; closed question শুধু confirmation দেয়।
Leading, trick বা double barrel প্রশ্ন এড়িয়ে চলুন।

example.en: In an IT class, the trainer asks why the file did not save. This open question starts discussion.

list_answer.title: Types of questions a facilitator can use
list_answer.title_bn: Facilitator যে ধরনের প্রশ্ন ব্যবহার করতে পারেন

items.text: Open questions: encourage participation; learners express their ideas and opinions.

cites.quote: Open questions These encourage participation and interaction.
learners to express their ideas and opinions.

items.text: Closed questions: used for confirmation; usually answered with Yes or No.

cites.quote: Closed questions These are used for confirmation. They are usually answered with Yes or No.

items.text: Direct questions: asked of a specific person or group to share expertise.

cites.quote: Direct questions These are asked of a specific person or group, and they encourage learners to share their expertise.

items.text: Indirect questions: open to everyone; learners choose their level of involvement.

cites.quote: Indirect questions These are open to everyone
Indirect questions allow learners to choose their level of involvement.

items.text: Leading questions: lead to the answer you are expecting or wanting.

cites.quote: Leading questions These lead to the answer you are expecting or wanting.

items.text: Factual questions: confirm knowledge; check if learners can recall facts.

cites.quote: Factual questions These are used to confirm knowledge, and can be used to check if learners can recall facts.

items.text: Probing questions: follow up answers without sufficient depth; always expressed as open questions.

cites.quote: Probing questions These are used to follow up answers that do not give sufficient depth/detail, and are always expressed as an open question.

items_bn: Open questions — participation বাড়ায়; learners নিজের ideas ও opinions খুলে বলতে পারে।
Closed questions — কিছু নিশ্চিত করতে (confirmation) ব্যবহার হয়; উত্তর সাধারণত Yes বা No।
Direct questions — নির্দিষ্ট কোনো ব্যক্তি বা group-কে করা হয়, যাতে তারা নিজের expertise ভাগ করে।
Indirect questions — সবার জন্য খোলা; কে কতটা অংশ নেবে, learners নিজেরাই বেছে নেয়।
Leading questions — প্রশ্নটাই learners-কে সেই উত্তরের দিকে নিয়ে যায়, যা আপনি আশা করছেন।
Factual questions — knowledge যাচাই করে; learners facts মনে করতে (recall) পারছে কিনা দেখে।
Probing questions — উত্তরে যথেষ্ট গভীরতা না থাকলে আরও জানতে পরের প্রশ্ন; সবসময় open question আকারে করা হয়।

short.prompt: Name the question types a facilitator can use, and the types to avoid.
short.modelAnswer:
Seven question types: open, closed, direct, indirect, leading, factual and probing.
Types of questions to avoid:
1. Leading questions
2. Double-barrel questions
3. Questions with unfamiliar terms
4. Irrelevant questions
5. Trick questions
6. Unethical questions
7. 'Too hard' or 'too easy' questions

keyPoints.text: Avoid leading, double-barrel, unfamiliar-term and irrelevant questions.

cites.quote: Types of questions to avoid • Leading questions • Double-barrel questions • Questions with unfamiliar terms • Irrelevant questions

keyPoints.text: Also avoid trick, unethical, and 'too hard' or 'too easy' questions.

cites.quote: Trick questions • Unethical questions • 'too hard' or 'too easy' questions

keyPoints.text: This is a leading question: 'Do you think it would be wise to seek advice?'

cites.quote: Leading questions These lead to the answer you are expecting or wanting. • Presumably you would check the safety requirements now? • I take it you have done this before? • Do you think it would be wise to seek advice before proceeding?

keyPoints.text: 'Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?' is a factual question.

cites.quote: Factual questions These are used to confirm knowledge, and can be used to check if learners can recall facts. • What are the four principles of assessment? • Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
